clue.text: Writer shares out novel development

indicators.note: a novel development is a new turn of events, so the letters of the two words take a new arrangement

explanation.surface: A writer hands out instalments of a novel as its plot develops.
explanation.walkthrough: 'novel development' signals that SHARES OUT is rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: A dated term for a female writer of books is the noun built on author with the feminine suffix.

clue.text: Fit girl given bodybuilding exercises

parts.note: Ada is a girl's name
PT stands for physical training, exercises that build up the body

explanation.surface: A fit young woman takes up a course of gym exercises.
explanation.definitionFit: As a verb, to fit something to a purpose is to modify or adjust it for that purpose.

clue.text: Delayed sailor with dire consequences

parts.note: tar is an old word for a sailor

indicators.note: the consequences of something are what it turns into, so the word dire is turned into a new order

explanation.surface: A sailor held back from duty suffers terrible results.
explanation.walkthrough: 'consequences' signals that DIRE is rearranged into RIED.
explanation.definitionFit: To tarry is to linger or stay too long, so the past tense means held up or delayed.

clue.text: One's put on weight — it's something in the air

indicators.note: placed after, so the word one follows the weight

parts.note: oz is the abbreviation for ounce, a unit of weight
one is taken as written; the 's stands for 'is'

explanation.surface: Someone who has put on weight blames something in the atmosphere.
explanation.definitionFit: A form of oxygen found in the atmosphere, and loosely used for bracing sea air.

clue.text: Impressions left by the dead

definitions.meaning: the ... of a speech or a picture are the impressions it makes
personal belongings bequeathed by someone who has died are called their personal ...

explanation.definitionFit: The plural noun covers both impressions made on an audience and the belongings a person leaves at death.

clue.text: Idiot — to get tight and then dance

parts.note: to screw something is to tighten it
a ball is a formal dance

explanation.surface: An idiot plans to get drunk and then go dancing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'tight' suggests drunk, but here it is the screw being tightened.
explanation.definitionFit: An eccentric or crazy person is called this, from the baseball pitch that breaks unpredictably.

clue.text: Flight path incomplete

indicators.note: the word for path loses its last letter, so it is not complete

parts.note: a route is a path taken

explanation.surface: A flight path that has not been fully plotted.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Flight' reads as aircraft travel, but it is the definition: a headlong retreat.
explanation.definitionFit: A disorderly retreat of a defeated army is a flight from the field.

clue.text: Soldier's uniform?

definitions.meaning: a professional soldier in a standing army is called a ...; the 's stands for 'is'
uniform as an adjective means even and consistent

explanation.definitionFit: The word names a career soldier in the standing army and, as an adjective, something even, steady and consistent.

clue.text: Restoration play in cut that's not normal

indicators.note: restoring is putting things back in order, so the letters of play in cut are arranged anew

explanation.surface: A Restoration comedy staged with a cut that is not usual.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Restoration play' looks like a period of English drama, but 'Restoration' is the signal to rearrange PLAY IN CUT.
explanation.definitionFit: A less common variant of atypical, meaning not representative or usual.

clue.text: Successfully manage an abduction?

definitions.meaning: to bring off a difficult task successfully
to abduct someone is to take them away by force

explanation.definitionFit: The phrasal verb means both to accomplish something with success and to take someone away by force.

clue.text: A man's entitled to them, but they're not left to son

definitions.text: A man's entitled to them, but they're not left to son

parts.words: A man's entitled to them, but they're not left to son
parts.note: things a person is entitled to are his entitlements; the second half plays on the opposite of left, as though these were not bequeathed to a son

explanation.surface: A father's entitlements are not passed on in his will.
explanation.definitionFit: Entitlements a person may lawfully claim, punning on the direction opposite to left.

clue.text: Bring the match alive with shot at goal

definitions.meaning: to light a match by rubbing it on the box
in football a shot at the goal is called this

explanation.definitionFit: The word means igniting a match by friction and, as a noun, a kick aimed at goal.

clue.text: Frighten with errors and bloomers

parts.note: to cow someone is to intimidate them
slips are small mistakes

explanation.surface: Someone scared by blunders and embarrassing gaffes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bloomers' looks like more errors (or underwear), but means flowers.
explanation.definitionFit: Yellow spring wildflowers of the primrose family are plants that bloom.

clue.text: Detectives in US agency retired, remaining sharp

indicators.note: the detectives go inside the agency's letters
having gone back, so the agency's letters run backwards

parts.note: CIA is the Central Intelligence Agency of the US
CID is the Criminal Investigation Department, the detective branch of British police

explanation.surface: Detectives working within a US agency stay keen after retirement.
explanation.walkthrough: 'retired' means gone back, so the agency is read backwards before the detectives go in. CID is the British police detective branch.
explanation.definitionFit: A sour, tart or biting taste or comment is described with this word for acid-like.

clue.text: Drink most commonly sold in bars

definitions.meaning: confectionery of cocoa is usually sold as bars

explanation.definitionFit: The cocoa product is both a hot drink and the confection sold in slabs.

clue.text: Put hold on the picture — it's a wrap!

indicators.note: the word for hold is placed on top of the picture in this down entry

parts.note: to cling is to grip tightly
a film is a motion picture

explanation.surface: A director halts shooting with the cry that filming is finished.
explanation.walkthrough: 'it's a wrap!' is what a director says at the end of filming; here it is literally a wrapping material.
explanation.definitionFit: Thin transparent plastic sheeting used for wrapping food.

clue.text: Put on heavy music symbolic of Ireland

parts.note: to sham is to feign or put on
rock is loud, heavy music

explanation.surface: Someone plays loud music to celebrate Irish identity.
explanation.definitionFit: The three-leaved clover is the national emblem of Ireland.

clue.text: The kindly feeling of its beneficiaries?

definitions.text: The kindly feeling of its beneficiaries?

parts.words: The kindly feeling of its beneficiaries?
parts.note: kindly feeling is benevolence; beneficiaries hint at people pleased with a generous testament leaving them money

explanation.surface: People who inherit money feel warmly towards the deceased.
explanation.definitionFit: Benevolence or friendly feeling, punning on a favourable legal testament.

clue.text: Lose wind when seeking muddy shoal in Cheshire estuary

indicators.note: the shoal goes inside the estuary's name

parts.note: the River Dee flows into an estuary on the Cheshire border of England and Wales
a flat is a stretch of low muddy ground exposed at low tide

explanation.surface: Walkers run out of breath looking for mudflats on a river in Cheshire.
explanation.walkthrough: The Dee is a river whose estuary runs between Cheshire (a county in north-west England) and Wales.
explanation.definitionFit: To let the air out of a tyre or balloon, so it loses its wind.

clue.text: T.S. Eliot play shows understatement

indicators.note: play suggests movement and looseness, so the poet's letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A drama by the poet T.S. Eliot is notable for restraint.
explanation.walkthrough: 'play' seems to be one of Eliot's dramas, but it signals rearranging TSELIOT.
explanation.definitionFit: A figure of speech using understatement, often by denying the opposite: 'not bad'.

clue.text: This by itself is only a gradual process

definitions.text: This by itself is only a gradual process

parts.words: This by itself is only a gradual process
parts.note: the word paired with itself either side of 'by' makes a phrase meaning gradually

explanation.surface: A remark that some change happens only slowly.
explanation.definitionFit: Doubled with 'by' between, the word forms the idiom for gradually, bit by bit.

clue.text: There's merit in unhappy endings

indicators.note: unhappy means disturbed, so the letters of merit in are disturbed

explanation.surface: A claim that sad endings to stories have artistic value.
explanation.walkthrough: 'unhappy' signals that MERIT IN is rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: End points of transport lines, or ends in general, using the Latin plural.

clue.text: Shadow boxing, a contest between fighters?

parts.note: to dog someone is to follow or shadow them
a fight is a boxing bout

explanation.surface: Shadow boxing described as a bout between two fighters.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Shadow boxing' reads as one training term, but splits into two words; 'fighters' are warplanes.
explanation.definitionFit: An aerial battle between fighter aircraft at close quarters.

clue.text: Feast on one's bed in the dormitory?

definitions.meaning: a cover for a bed is a bedspread

explanation.definitionFit: The word means a lavish meal and, short for bedspread, a cover on a bed.

clue.text: Describing a boom in the travel industry once

definitions.text: Describing a boom in the travel industry once

parts.words: Describing a boom in the travel industry once
parts.note: a boom is the bang an aircraft makes breaking the sound barrier, as Concorde once did, not an economic surge

explanation.surface: An account of a past period of growth in tourism.
explanation.definitionFit: Relating to sound; a boom from a supersonic airliner like Concorde is described with this adjective.

clue.text: Share out a tax rise

indicators.note: in a down entry a rise means the letters read upwards

parts.note: a toll is a charge or tax for using a road or bridge

explanation.surface: A tax increase is shared among the people.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue 'rise' means the tax word is read from the bottom up, after the A given as written.
explanation.definitionFit: To allot is to distribute or apportion shares.

clue.text: Italian banger unfortunately going the wrong way joining the motorway

indicators.note: the motorway attaches after the reversed piece
travelling backwards, so the word is read in reverse

parts.note: alas is an exclamation of misfortune
the M1, written MI, is Britain's main north-south motorway

explanation.surface: A driver going the wrong way joins a motorway, a banger of a car.
explanation.walkthrough: 'going the wrong way' turns ALAS into SALA. A banger is British slang for a sausage (and an old car); the M1 is a motorway out of London.
explanation.definitionFit: A cured spiced sausage originating in Italy.

clue.text: Substantial list includes gin cocktail

indicators.note: the list holds the mixed letters inside it

parts.note: a table is a listed arrangement of data

indicators.note: a cocktail is a mixture, so the letters of gin are mixed

explanation.surface: A long drinks list featuring a gin cocktail.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cocktail' mixes the letters of the spirit before 'includes' places them within the list; 'gin cocktail' seems to be a drink on the surface.
explanation.definitionFit: Something real and solid enough to be touched is substantial.

clue.text: A venerable name in our illustrious past

definitions.text: A venerable name in our illustrious past

parts.words: A venerable name in our illustrious past
parts.note: the Anglo-Saxon monk and historian known by the title the Venerable

explanation.surface: A tribute to a revered figure from English history.
explanation.definitionFit: The eighth-century Northumbrian monk and historian is traditionally titled the Venerable.

clue.text: Stomach is churning — but he enjoys it!

indicators.note: a churning stomach is turned over and over, so its letters are mixed

explanation.surface: A man whose stomach heaves still takes pleasure in it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'churning' signals that STOMACH IS is rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who takes pleasure in their own pain or suffering, so he enjoys the discomfort.
